'''''Corylus maxima''''', the '''filbert''', is a species of [[hazel]] in the [[birch family]]. It is [[native plant|native]] to Eurasia and produces an edible nut.

== Description ==
It is a [[deciduous]] [[shrub]] {{convert|6-10|m|abbr=off}} tall, with [[plant stem|stems]] up to {{convert|20|cm|0|abbr=off}} thick. The [[leaves]] are rounded, {{convert|5-12|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} long by {{convert|4–10|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} broad, with a coarsely double-serrated margin.

The [[flower]]s are [[Anemophily|wind-pollinated]] [[catkin]]s produced in late winter. The [[male]] ([[pollen]]) catkins are pale yellow, {{convert|5–10|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} long, while the [[female]] catkins are bright red and only {{convert|1–3|mm|frac=16|abbr=on}} long. The [[fruit]] is a [[nut (fruit)|nut]] produced in clusters of 1–5 together. Each nut is {{convert|1.5–2.5|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} long, fully enclosed in a {{convert|3–5|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} long, tubular [[bract#Involucral bracts|involucre]] ([[husk]]).<ref name="rushforth">Rushforth, K. (1999). ''Trees of Britain and Europe''. Collins {{ISBN|0-00-220013-9}}.{{Page needed|date=August 2025}}</ref><ref name="fnwe">Flora of NW Europe: [http://ip30.eti.uva.nl/BIS/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=1776 ''Corylus maxima''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090508050151/http://ip30.eti.uva.nl/BIS/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=1776 |date=2009-05-08 }}</ref>

=== Similar species ===

The filbert is similar to the related common hazel, ''[[Corylus avellana|C. avellana]]'', differing in having the nut more fully enclosed by the tubular [[Bract|involucre]]. This feature is shared by the beaked hazel ''[[Corylus cornuta|C. cornuta]]'' of North America, and the Asian beaked hazel ''[[Corylus sieboldiana|C. sieboldiana]]'' of eastern Asia.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is [[native plant|native]] to southeastern Europe and southwestern Asia, from the Balkans to Ordu in Turkey.<ref name="rushforth" />

==Uses==

The filbert nut is edible and is very similar to the [[hazelnut]] (cobnut). Its main use in the United States is as large filler (along with peanuts as small filler) in most containers of mixed nuts. Filberts are sometimes grown in [[orchard]]s for the nuts, but much less often than the common hazel.<ref name=rushforth/><ref name=fnwe/>

The purple-leaved [[cultivar]] ''C. maxima'' 'Purpurea' is a popular [[Ornamental plant|ornamental shrub]] in gardens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Corylus maxima'' 'Purpurea' |url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=555 |access-date=19 July 2013}}</ref>

==Name==
In [[Oregon]], "filbert" is used for commercial hazelnuts in general. Use in this manner has faded partly due to the efforts of Oregon's hazelnut growers to brand their product to better appeal to global markets and avoid confusion.<ref>[http://www.oregonhazelnuts.org/ Oregon Hazelnut Marketing Board]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.oda.state.or.us/information/AQ/AQFall99/07.html|title=Agriculture Quarterly - Oregon Department of Agriculture|website=www.oda.state.or.us}}</ref>

The etymology for 'filbert' may trace to Norman French. [[Saint Philibert]]'s feast day is 20 August (old style) and the plant was possibly renamed after him because the nuts were mature on this day.<ref>''[[Oxford English Dictionary]]''.</ref>{{full citation needed|date=October 2024}}
